key_votes.title: Baldwin amendment: shield Medicaid funding
key_votes.question: On the Amendment S.Amdt. 1693 to H.Con.Res. 14 (2025 budget resolution)
key_votes.yes_means: Yes was a vote to add a budget reserve fund aimed at preventing Medicaid funding cuts that could close rural hospitals, raise costs for people with other insurance, or increase uncompensated care.

key_votes.title: House passes H.R. 1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act
key_votes.question: On Passage of H.R. 1
key_votes.yes_means: Yes was a vote to pass the House version of the 2025 budget reconciliation bill. Its health provisions included new Medicaid work requirements and limits on how states finance their share of Medicaid.

key_votes.title: Kim amendment: strike H.R. 1's limits on Medicaid payments
key_votes.question: On the Amendment S.Amdt. 2817 to H.R. 1
key_votes.yes_means: Yes was a vote to remove the bill's limits on certain Medicaid payments to states and providers.

key_votes.title: Sanders amendment: halve Medicare drug prices, add dental, vision and hearing
key_votes.question: On the Amendment S.Amdt. 2435 to H.R. 1
key_votes.yes_means: Yes was a vote to cut prescription drug prices under Medicare in half and expand Medicare to cover dental, vision and hearing.

key_votes.title: Senate passes H.R. 1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act
key_votes.question: On Passage of the Bill H.R. 1
key_votes.yes_means: Yes was a vote to pass the 2025 budget reconciliation bill, which added Medicaid work requirements and limits on state Medicaid financing. It passed 50-50 with the Vice President breaking the tie.

key_votes.title: House gives final approval to H.R. 1
key_votes.question: On Motion to Concur in the Senate Amendment to H.R. 1
key_votes.yes_means: Yes was a vote to send the Senate-passed budget reconciliation bill, with its Medicaid work requirements and financing limits, to the President to become law.

key_votes.title: Extend the expanded ACA premium tax credits
key_votes.question: On the Cloture Motion to proceed to S. 3385
key_votes.yes_means: Yes was a vote to move forward a bill extending the enhanced premium tax credits that lower the cost of Affordable Care Act marketplace insurance. It needed 60 votes and got 51.

issue_polls.stat: 35% pick inflation/prices as their most important issue, roughly triple the next-highest issues (health care and jobs/economy, 12% each)
58% of registered voters are extremely concerned about inflation; about 6 in 10 name cost of living as their top economic worry
66% call inflation a very big problem for the country, up from 63% a year earlier
In the open-ended most important problem question, 17% named inflation and 38% named some economic issue
73% say the affordability of health care is a very big problem, up 6 points from February 2025
61% worry a great deal about health care access and affordability, the highest of 16 domestic issues tested
66% worry about affording health care; 67% say Congress did the wrong thing by not extending enhanced ACA tax credits
66% say the federal government is responsible for ensuring all Americans have health coverage; 35% favor a single national government program and 31% a mix of government and private programs
74% say the role of money in politics is a very big problem, the top item of 13 tested, with majorities in both parties agreeing
60% of registered voters are extremely concerned about government corruption, the highest of 13 issues tested
81% of registered voters support banning members of Congress from trading stocks
29% think most people running the government are corrupt and another 53% think many are
50% of registered voters call the economy extremely important to their midterm vote, tied for the top of 11 issues
51% worry a great deal about the economy; 35% worry a great deal about unemployment

35% of registered voters call crime extremely important to their midterm vote

issue_polls.stat: 80% of voters say working parents' ability to find and afford child care is a crisis or major problem

issue_polls.pollster: UpOne Insight for First Five Years Fund
issue_polls.stat: 62% support sending federal child care funds to states through a block grant
46% worry a great deal about hunger and homelessness
44% worry a great deal about global warming, among the highest readings since 1989
39% say climate change is a very big problem for the country
29% of registered voters call climate change extremely important to their midterm vote, the lowest of 11 issues
43% worry a great deal about the Social Security system
32% of registered voters are extremely concerned about AI technology
30% of registered voters call construction of AI data centers extremely important to their midterm vote
52% are more concerned than excited about increased AI use in daily life (up from 37% in 2021); 71% expect AI to mean fewer U.S. jobs over 20 years
71% oppose building an AI data center in their area, including 48% strongly opposed
35% of registered voters call the Israeli-Palestinian situation extremely important to their midterm vote
41% sympathize more with Palestinians and 36% with Israelis; 57% favor creating an independent Palestinian state
6% of registered voters name tariffs as their top economic worry

45% worry a great deal about the size and power of the federal government
40% worry a great deal about the possibility of terrorist attacks

exit_national.stat: Economy was named the most important issue facing the country by 39% of voters, followed by state of democracy at 32%.
Preliminary exit polls put immigration at 14%, health care 8%, foreign policy 4% and crime 3% as most important issue (pollster not named in the write-up).
exit_national.source: Winston Group summary of preliminary exit polls

exit_national.stat: About 4 in 10 voters named the economy as top issue, roughly 3 in 10 state of democracy, and about 1 in 10 each immigration and health care.
More than 80% of voters said they were worried about prices of health care (along with gas, groceries, utilities).
Voters favored Democrats over Republicans on handling health care by 19 points, 49% to 30%, versus a 7-point Harris edge on this in 2024.
exit_national.source: KFF analysis of the 2026 Voter Poll (SSRS)

exit_national.stat: 54% said Trump administration policies made their own health care costs worse and 10% said better; those saying worse backed Democratic House candidates 82% to 16%.
exit_national.source: KFF analysis of the 2026 Voter Poll (SSRS)

exit_national.stat: 30% of voters said they support the MAHA movement, 39% do not, and 31% did not know enough.
Democrats won independents by 22 points nationally, and independents were 33% of the electorate (pollster not named in the article).
